ratings_why.fun: Winding the moon to choose your shop phase and fight phase is a real plan each turn, and the Tier 6 fork between Meikle Care and Grandam gives the late game two shapes; turns 4 to 6 can feel blank without Moon-Gazers.
ratings_why.distinct: A visible, windable shared clock plus Borrow as a doubling layer over other tribes plays unlike any of today's tribes, though phase triggers alone are a familiar idea.

verdict_why: One real rules hole (Longshanks' endless bout) and one trigger-order question need a line each; the growth shape is otherwise ready.

points.text: Under the moon Jill Longshanks takes no damage, so a bout against an enemy she can't hurt (Damage Reduction at or above her Attack) never ends. Add an end, such as 'after 5 hits each, the bout ends'.
A Ribboned Jack borrowing Almanac Jill: both fire on one Hare play, the first turns the moon off Full, and it's unclear whether the Jack's already-triggered copy still resolves. Say which.
Between turn 3's and turn 7's natural Full, most Tier 1-2 text is idle unless you hold Moon-Gazers. A Tier 2 Waning or Waxing payoff would give the early off-phase turns something to do.

Mother Meikle Care's Full trigger has no Once a turn, so each extra Full bought with Moon-Gazers pays the whole board again. That makes gold the late-game dial, which is a fun shape; keep it, and let sims set the price.
Grandam of the Forms copying The Moon-Scour gives two Once-a-turn Scours, which doubles the tribe's steepest curve. A great high roll; worth showing in a build line so players chase it.

standouts.why: Old Wat is a free moon turn every shop that costs a hand slot, and with Almanac Jill a second one; cheap, readable and true to the lore.
The Three Hares turns every permanent Full payout into a positional puzzle, a clean Tier 4 multiplier.
Grandam makes the back row of Leverets pay off into copies and triples, a capstone the comp is clearly built to reach.

weakest.why: Witch in Borrowed Shape works only in Full fights, depends on what the enemy put across, and opponents see the Full coming.
Silver Sixpence Doe pays 2 gold once per natural moon cycle unless you build hard for New, thin for a Tier 2 economy piece.
Ribboned Jack is a vanilla 3/3 outside Full and only reads its left neighbour, so it's often blank.

flags.note: The Moon-Scour's counter grows with every Full, including Fulls bought with gold under Meikle Care, so its payout grows roughly with the square of the turn; with Waxwell it can pass the Tier 6 top by a lot.
Meikle Care plus Waxwell plus Ring Referee turns each extra Full into about +12/+12 per Hare, limited only by gold and Moon-Gazer supply.
Grandam's copies count towards triples and each triple Discovers; Once a turn and back-row space cap it, but a triple chain every two turns is possible.
The Moonlit bout has no end when she can't damage the target.
